clue.text: Very good Austen novel when keeping quiet in the afternoon

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the quiet sign sits within the other pieces

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good
Emma is a novel by Jane Austen
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a Jane Austen book in silence during a quiet afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: PIP EMMA is old military signallers' slang for PM, the letters P and M being spoken as 'pip' and 'emma'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pip emma is the signallers' spoken form of PM, the abbreviation for times after noon.

clue.text: Old boy restricted by disease — one gets lots of letters

indicators.note: being restricted by something means being hemmed in by it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: pox is a general word for a disease
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil is laid up with an illness, while someone else receives piles of post.
explanation.definitionFit: A post office box is a mailbox rented at a post office, where an addressee's letters collect.

clue.text: Devastation in small community with new leader

indicators.note: a new leader means the first letter of the word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: a village is a small community

explanation.surface: A little settlement is wrecked, then gets a new head.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter replaces the V; the answer's meaning settles it as P.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillage is plundering and laying waste, so it is a synonym of devastation.

clue.text: PM once having a supernatural power?

parts.note: Theresa May was once the UK Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A question whether a former Prime Minister had magical abilities.
explanation.walkthrough: PM is Prime Minister; Theresa May led the UK government 2016-19.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu thought maya is illusion, the magical power by which gods make the visible world appear.

clue.text: Thrown overboard, Magnus — huge figure

indicators.note: thrown suggests the letters are tossed about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Magnus gets pitched off a ship, and he is a big fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown' rearranges OVERBOARD and MAGNUS. 'Huge figure' looks like a description of Magnus but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Avogadro's number, about six times ten to the twenty-third, is an enormous constant in chemistry.

clue.text: Bad booze endlessly knocked back as contraband?

parts.note: ill can mean bad, as in ill effects

indicators.note: knocked back means turned round, so the letters run backwards here
endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: lager is a type of booze

explanation.surface: Smuggled drink, downed in quantity, is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests drinking, but it reverses LAGE ('endlessly' trims the booze) to EGAL. The question mark admits contraband is used as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraband goods are those banned by law, so as an adjective contraband means unlawful.

clue.text: Nearing the end of the holiday, everything else having gone wrong?

definitions.text: Nearing the end of the holiday
definitions.meaning: read literally, at the final resort on a tour of holiday towns
the idiom means when all other options have failed

explanation.surface: A traveller's trip is closing, and nothing has worked out.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a final fallback once every alternative is exhausted, and also literally means staying at the last holiday town visited.

clue.text: Girl, a female always getting a nasty illness

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl
ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A young woman keeps catching a horrible bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassa fever is a dangerous viral haemorrhagic disease found in West Africa.

clue.text: Wicked rogues pinching 500 dollars in Haiti

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing hold of, so the letters close around the extra piece
wicked suggests the letters behave badly and are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Villains steal a sum of money in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' rearranges ROGUES to GOURES, and 'pinching' takes D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The gourde is Haiti's currency, the local counterpart of the dollar.

clue.text: Lake Superior has trees and American flowers

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
U stands for upper class, so superior
pines are trees

explanation.surface: The shores of Lake Superior carry conifers and native blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lake Superior' looks like the Great Lake but splits into L and U.
explanation.definitionFit: Lupines is the American spelling of lupins, tall garden plants with spikes of blossom.

clue.text: Charge enemy finally — viciously attack male beast

parts.note: a bill is a charge to be paid

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: to go at someone is to attack them fiercely

explanation.surface: A command to rush the foe and assault a male animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A billy goat is a male goat, so a male animal.

clue.text: Dismiss puzzle — must pee

indicators.note: to puzzle is to confuse, so the letters are muddled into a new order

parts.note: pee is how the letter P is said

explanation.surface: Someone is baffled why they urgently need the loo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puzzle' looks like a second definition but is the anagram signal, turning MUST into STUM. In cricket, a batter is dismissed by being stumped.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the wicketkeeper can stump a batter, putting them out by breaking the wicket.

clue.text: Chinese city Christian?

definitions.meaning: ... is a city in central China
An abbreviation for Christian, the X being the Greek letter chi

explanation.surface: Asking if a Chinese city is a believer.
explanation.definitionFit: Xi'an is the old capital of Shaanxi, and Xian is an informal short form for a follower of Christ.

clue.text: An animal sound in outdoor area? One may take note of that

definitions.text: One may take note of that

indicators.note: in places one piece within another, here the article and cry go inside the outdoor space

parts.note: a garden is an outdoor area
mew is a cat's cry

explanation.surface: A cat cries in the yard, and someone notices it.
explanation.definitionFit: A game warden supervises wildlife, so notices animals and their cries.

clue.text: Bird certain to fly around river and around end of forest

indicators.note: around means the scrambled word wraps the following pieces
to fly suggests the letters scatter and settle in a new order

parts.note: C, for circa, means around

indicators.note: end of points to the closing letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A bird is sure to fly over a river and round the edge of a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fly' rearranges CERTAIN to AICTERN; the first 'around' places it about R, C and T. The second 'around' is C (circa).
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic tern is a seabird famous for the longest migration of any bird.

clue.text: The woman's covering part of body — what is that part?

indicators.note: covering means surrounding, so the pronoun wraps the body part

parts.note: her is the woman's
the ear is a part of the body

explanation.surface: A woman shields some part of herself, and someone asks which part.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers back to the ear just named: an ear is something that hears.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of listening is literally a hearer, one that perceives sounds.

clue.text: Being germ-free, is almost passed for work

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or rework it, so the letters are reshaped
almost means the final letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: Being clean of infection almost gets one through at the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims PASSED to PASSE; 'work' rearranges IS plus PASSE. 'Work' looks like a noun about employment.
explanation.definitionFit: Asepsis is the absence of harmful microbes, the sterile condition of an operating theatre.

clue.text: Rodents 'orrible woman has in the open on island

parts.note: 'ag is hag with the h dropped, matching the dropped h of 'orrible
out means in the open, known publicly

explanation.surface: A dreadful woman keeps small animals outdoors on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of ''orrible' signals that the hag also loses her H.
explanation.definitionFit: Agoutis are burrowing rodents of Central and South America, related to guinea pigs.

clue.text: Bowing as a group around church

indicators.note: around means the group encloses the church abbreviation

parts.note: a ring is a group, as in a spy ring

explanation.surface: A congregation bends low together around a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Arching means curving, as a back bends when bowing.

clue.text: Make faster progress than unfashionable people

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Untrendy folk move ahead more quickly than others.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrace is to beat in speed, going quicker than a rival.

clue.text: Get a round going? Drink not available, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are judged by how they sound

parts.note: tea off would mean tea is off the menu, not available

explanation.surface: Someone tries to order a round at the bar, but there is nothing to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' suggests buying drinks, but it is a round of golf, begun by teeing off.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, players tee off to play the first stroke and so start a round.

clue.text: Loud user of tongue in a flash

parts.note: f (forte) is the musical marking for loud
a licker uses the tongue

explanation.surface: A noisy talker speaks up in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'user of tongue' suggests a talker, but it is someone licking.
explanation.definitionFit: A flicker is a brief flash of light, a momentary gleam.

clue.text: In Christian Union teach odd chaps — this convert is still learning

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, here the scrambled letters go within the union's initials

parts.note: CU is the abbreviation for Christian Union, a student society

indicators.note: odd suggests strangeness, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: chaps are men

explanation.surface: Within a student Christian group, strange men instruct a new believer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' seems to describe the chaps but rearranges the verb, giving ATECH. The Christian Union is a student religious society found at British universities.
explanation.definitionFit: A catechumen is someone receiving instruction in Christianity before baptism.

clue.text: Passes time in classical fashion

explanation.surface: Time slips by the way the ancients reckoned it.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who passes away is deceased, and in Latin the noun for day, a unit of time, is dies.

clue.text: Instrument with arrows pointing north

indicators.note: in a down answer pointing north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: darts are small arrows

explanation.surface: A device with arrows aiming upward, like a compass.
explanation.definitionFit: A Strad, short for Stradivarius, is a violin made by Antonio Stradivari.

clue.text: Spirit abuse needs to be cut by half

indicators.note: cut by half means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: to maltreat is to abuse

explanation.surface: Alcohol misuse has to be reduced by fifty per cent.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt is short for malt whisky, a spirit distilled from malted barley.

clue.text: One judge is far from happy

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A judge is described as quite unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means angry, which is well removed from contentment.

clue.text: Man bitten by dog? One may indicate disease

indicators.note: bitten by means held in the jaws, so the dog wraps the other piece

parts.note: a barker is a dog
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man is bitten by a dog and someone wonders about infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man, a British Crown dependency.
explanation.definitionFit: A biomarker is a measurable biological sign used to detect or diagnose illness.

clue.text: Good student losing heart, one gathers

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a learner is a student

explanation.surface: A fine pupil gets discouraged as someone collects things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' removes the central R of LEARNER, leaving LEANER.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleaner collects leftover crops after harvest, so is a gatherer.

clue.text: Taught nothing revolutionary after expression of disapproval

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come later than the disapproving sound

parts.note: tut is a sound of disapproval
O looks like zero, so nothing
red means a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: Someone was instructed in nothing radical, after a tut of disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutored means instructed by a private teacher, so taught.
